'''''Eryngium pandanifolium''''', or '''pandan-like-leaved eryngo''' or '''caraguata''', is a species of flowering plant in the genus ''[[Eryngium]]'' of the family [[Apiaceae]], native to southern Brazil, Paraguay, Uruguay, and Argentina, and introduced in Australia, New Zealand,<ref name="841950-1" >{{cite web |url=http://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:841950-1 |title=''Eryngium pandanifolium'' Cham. & Schltdl. |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=2017 |website=Plants of the World Online |publisher=Board of Trustees of the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew |access-date=20 February 2021 }}</ref> and Portugal. It has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref>{{cite web |title=''Eryngium pandanifolium'' pandan-like-leaved eryngo |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/32556/Eryngium-pandanifolium/Details |publisher=The Royal Horticultural Society |access-date=20 February 2021 }}</ref> Its leaves, which closely resemble those of the unrelated Pampas grass (''[[Cortaderia]]'') are up to {{cvt|2.7|m}} long<ref>Gardener's Chronicle, volume 26 (second series) 16 October 1886 p. 496</ref> while only {{cvt|2.5|to|5|cm}} wide.

==Subtaxa==
The following varieties are currently accepted:<ref name="841950-1" />
*''Eryngium pandanifolium'' var. ''chamissonis'' <small>(Urb.) Mathias & Constance</small>
*''Eryngium pandanifolium'' var. ''lassauxii'' <small>(Decne.) Mathias & Constance</small>

==Invasive species==
''Eryngium pandanifolium'' is legally classified as an invasive species in Portugal since 1999. It has settled in damp areas around the [[Tagus]] and [[Mondego River|Mondego]] river basins.<ref>{{cite web |title=ryngium pandanifolium Cham. & Schltdl. |url=https://flora-on.pt/?q=Eryngium+pandanifolium |publisher=[[Flora-On]] |access-date=3 December 2022}}</ref>
